What are the specifications of a power supply unit (PSU)?
2025-05-29
Choosing a PSU usually starts with selecting the form factor. Standard desktop systems commonly use ATX, while compact builds may opt for SFX or TFX. Next, you can choose the efficiency rating and determine the required wattage based on the components used.
What is ATX 3.0?
2025-05-29
ATX 3.0 is a desktop Power Supply Design Guide that Intel updated in 2022, in which new versions of design specifications such as CPU 12V current configuration and Peak Load requirements are included.
What is ATX 3.1?
2025-05-29
ATX 3.1 is a desktop power supply design guide updated by Intel in September 2023. It references the PCIe 5.1 specification and updates the 12+4 pin 12VHPWR connector to 12V-2x6.
What’s the difference between ATX 3.0 and ATX 3.1?
2025-05-29
The 12+4 pin 12VHPWR connector has been updated to 12V-2x6 with optimized physical structure
Hold up time (T5+T6) specification changed to >12 ms
-12V is no longer required (Required → Recommended)
How will PCIe Gen 5 impact the system that I am currently using?
2025-05-29
If the gaming system is not equipped with a standalone graphics card, it will have no impact.
If it is equipped with the new specification PCIe Gen 5, new optional power needs to be purchased that can provide a new version of PCIe 12V-2x6 (12VHPWR) cable and a design that allows instantaneous power to reach up to 200%.
Do FSP power supplies support PCIe Gen 5? What’s the product launching plan?
2025-05-29
1. FSP had started laying out and did R&D on PCIe Gen 5 powers since 2020-2021, and is now manufacturing PCIe Gen 5 power supply.
2. FSP has launched its PCIe Gen 5 power supply in Q4 of 2022. All products to comply with Intel PSDG ATX 3.0 and 12VO 2.0 specifications. Power supplies grater than 450W meet Peak Load 200% design. Power supplies less than or equal to 450W meet Peak Load 150% design. New version of PCIe 12VHPWR cable plans to be included as a standard accessory with power supplies with 750W (included) or above. For power supplies less than 750W, it will be configured according to customer’s requirements.
What is PCIe Gen 5?
2025-05-29
Prior to PCI Express CEM 5.0, the specifications did not allow any tolerance for add-in cards to exceed their rated power limits, which could trigger power supply overcurrent protection mechanisms. PCIe CEM 5.0 defines power excursion specifications, and ATX 3.0 follows the same guidelines to support next-generation graphics cards.
How to choose a suitable PC power supply? What factors to consider?
2026-05-04
Evaluate based on five core metrics:
Wattage: Aim for 1.2-1.5 times the total system power consumption.
Standard: ATX 3.0/3.1 is highly recommended for high-end GPUs.
Efficiency: Prioritize 80 PLUS Gold or higher.
Build quality: Look for 105°C Japanese capacitors and DC-DC architecture.
Cables & Size: Full modularity and chassis compatibility (ATX/SFX).
Why does my PC constantly trip or shut down?
2026-05-04
Common reasons include:
OPP/OCP triggered by GPU power spikes.
OTP (Over-Temperature Protection) due to poor airflow or dust.
Voltage instability/Aging capacitors causing high ripple.
External grid issues: Bad outlets or brownouts. If protection triggers, turn off the switch and wait 1 minute before restarting.
PSU specs and voltage selection? Can it support my GPU?
2026-05-04
To ensure GPU compatibility, check:
Voltage matching: Must support Full Range input, with a highly stable +12V rail.
+12V capacity: The +12V wattage should be very close to the PSU's total rated power.
Physical cables: ATX 3.1 PSUs with native 12V-2x6 cables are recommended for new GPUs.
Power Excursion: ATX 3.0/3.1 handles 200% power spikes; older ATX 2.4 units need 200-300W of extra headroom.
How to determine if a PSU supports high-end GPUs or multi-monitor setups?
2026-05-04
Do not just look at total wattage; evaluate four aspects:
+12V output must be close to total rated power.
For multi-monitor power spikes, an ATX 3.1 certified PSU with native 12V-2x6 interfaces is highly recommended.
Avoid using daisy-chained PCIe split cables.
Choose DC-DC and Japanese capacitor designs for low-ripple, clean power.
The power indicator light is on, but the PC won't boot. How to fix it?
2026-05-04
Check the warranty. If under warranty, contact the manufacturer/dealer for repair or replacement. If out of warranty and older than 5 years, we recommend upgrading to an ATX 3.1 compliant PSU for safety and efficiency.
Can I replace my desktop power supply with any random one?
2026-05-04
Absolutely not! Before replacing, verify:
Never mix modular cables: Pinouts vary; mixing them can burn out hardware instantly.
Check Form Factor (ATX / SFX / Proprietary).
Check ATX standard (new GPUs need ATX 3.1).
Do not downgrade wattage, and aim for 80 PLUS Gold efficiency level.
How often should a desktop PC power supply be replaced?
2026-05-04
Evaluate based on "warranty period" and "hardware upgrades":
Capacitor aging: Entry-level PSUs should be replaced every 3-5 years; high-end units with Japanese caps last 7-10 years.
Hardware upgrades: When upgrading to a high-end GPU, if your PSU is >5 years old, upgrade to ATX 3.1.
Replace immediately if you notice abnormal noises, burning smells, random reboots, or severe coil whine.
